# Same transform, different ownership

[A local transform and a distributed transform can share an interface without sharing an ownership policy.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

Example 09 previously filled a manually decomposed field with random
values and printed a transform. Here the data are deterministic, the field
is explicitly bound to the transform's real-space inbox, and the inverse
checks that values survive either implementation.

## Count the real and complex values

The real grid has $16\times8\times4=512$ values. Conjugate symmetry for
real input permits the x-half Fourier spectrum,

$$
(16/2+1)\times8\times4=288
$$ {#eq-half}

complex values. The x-Nyquist plane is included. This storage convention
must be accounted for when applying Fourier symbols; it is not a second,
smaller physical domain [@trefethen2000, program 5].

## Ask the transform for its layout

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="layouts" dedent=4}
```

The stack's `u` uses its FFT inbox. The coefficient vector uses
`size_outbox()`. A distributed transform can redistribute values between
those layouts, so deriving one layout by guessing from the other is unsafe.

`IHostFFT` defines the common transform contract. `Implementation::Local`
selects a complete-domain FFTW transform and requires one communicator
rank. `Implementation::Heffte` supports distributed ownership. Neither
choice here selects a GPU backend.

## Two runs of the same program

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
```

The supplied JSON selects `"implementation": "heffte"`. Change it to
`"local"` and repeat. Both should report the totals in @eq-half and a
round-trip error near floating-point roundoff.

Now select HeFFTe and use `--ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun`. The global totals
stay the same. Try the local implementation with two ranks: it should be
rejected rather than silently running two unrelated copies of the global
problem. That failure control is part of the numerical check.

## What this comparison does and does not measure

This is a contract and layout demonstration. It records no timing and
makes no performance recommendation. The original signal
$1+\cos(3x)$ is a small resolved mode; the
[coefficient lesson](../round-trip/index.qmd) provides an independent DFT
comparison instead of relying only on a round trip.

See the [local FFT contract](https://github.com/ahojukka5/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/fft/local_fft.hpp)
and [host FFT interface](https://github.com/ahojukka5/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/fft/fft_interface.hpp)
for ownership, normalization and lifetime details.

The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson.
